novelty.justification: The new relationship proposed is that an "attention-implemented variable-binding mechanism" has a capacity that "sets a hard limit on how many entities a model can track," with near-limit failures dominated by role-filler swaps and shared across coreference and reasoning. Searches for “transformer entity binding binding-ID subspace causal swap,” “attention variable binding working-memory capacity,” and “entity tracking attention heads capacity” identify Feng and Steinhardt’s How Do Language Models Bind Entities in Context? as the closest established work on low-dimensional binding IDs and causal rebinding, while Attention as Binding (2025) and Structured-Sparse Attention for Entity Tracking (2026) respectively anticipate the vector-symbolic framing and a collapse when tracked properties exceed attention heads. Turning those ingredients into a cross-task binding-capacity law with swap-error and architectural-scaling predictions is a non-trivial operationalization, but it is a natural extension and combination of prior mechanisms rather than a new core interpretability paradigm.
